shared_elements: shallow low-relief animal in profile carved on pillar face
repeated row of small carved units forming a horizontal band (pit/cupmark row vs arcaded row)
justification: Both show pale worked limestone monoliths bearing shallow, flat-bottomed relief — most specifically a small quadruped in profile on the pillar face in A echoing the profile beasts in B, plus a repeated row of small identical units (pitted cupmarks in A, arcaded figures in B) reading as a horizontal band. The decisive difference is density and framing: B is a close view of a single densely programmed surface with stacked registers, while A is a wide excavation view of mostly blank, undecorated stones scattered across a trench, so no comparable composition exists.
